questions.question: The main items of ________ expenditure are interest payments, defence services, subsidies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**non-plan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main items of **non-plan expenditure** are** interest payments, defence services, subsidies.**
 
• Non-plan expenditure refers to the **regular expenses** incurred by the government, which are not related to any specific plan or project.
 
• Interest payments include the **interest paid on loans** taken by the government, such as external debt and domestic debt.
 
• Defence services include expenses related to the **maintenance and modernization of armed forces**, as well as the payment of salaries and pensions to defence personnel.
 
• Subsidies include various types of **subsidies given by the government,** such as food subsidies, fertilizer subsidies, and fuel subsidies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waste expenditure** refers to the expenses incurred on activities that** do not **contribute to the welfare of society, such as corruption and unnecessary administrative expenses.
 
• **Plan expenditure** refers to the expenses incurred on **specific plans or projects**, such as infrastructure development and poverty alleviation.
 
• **Household expenditure** refers to the expenses incurred by households on various** goods and services,** such as food, clothing, and housing.

questions.question: Which classical dance generally narrates the story of the feminine form of Vishnu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniattam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniattam **is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Kerala, India.**
 
• It is a dance form that is mainly **performed by women** and is known for its graceful movements and expressions.
 
• The dance form generally narrates the story of the** feminine form of Vishnu**, which is **Mohini.**
 
• Mohini is believed to be the female avatar of Lord Vishnu, who is often depicted as a** beautiful woman** with **enchanting powers.**
 
• The dance form is characterized by** slow, swaying movements, and intricate footwork,** which is accompanied by **music and poetry.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Assam,** India.

 
 
• It is known for its **devotional themes** and is performed mainly by **male dancers.**
 
 
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form that originated in **North India** and is known for its fast footwork and intricate hand gestures.
 
 
• It is a dance form that narrates stories from **Hindu mythology.**
 
 
 
• **Manipuri** is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Manipur**, India.
 
 
• It is known for its graceful movements and is performed mainly by **women**.
 
• It generally narrates stories from the life of **Lord Krishna.**

questions.question: India has a parliamentary form of government which is a feature borrowed from the ________ Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __** Britain.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's parliamentary form **of government is heavily influenced by the **British parliamentary **system, which was introduced during the** colonial period.**
 
• The Indian Constitution lays down the framework for the parliamentary system, which is based on the **Westminster model **of the British Parliament.
 
• The Indian Parliament consists of two houses, the **Lok Sabha **and the **Rajya Sabha, **which are similar to the **House of Commons** and the **House of Lords** in the **British Parliament.**
 
• The **Indian Prime Minister** is the **head of the government** and is selected by the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha, similar to the role of the British Prime Minister.
 
• The British Constitution is an **unwritten constitution**, which means that it is **not codified** in a single document.
 
• Instead, it is based on a collection of **laws, customs, and conventions** that have evolved over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **South Africa **has a parliamentary system of government, but it is **not** based on the British model.

 
 
• The South African Constitution was adopted in **1996 **and is a hybrid of **parliamentary and presidential** systems.
 
 
 
• The **United States** has a** presidential system** of government, which is based on the separation of powers between the **executive, legislative, and judicial branches** of government.
 
 
• The US Constitution was adopted in **1787** and is the **oldest written** constitution in the world.
 
 
 
• **Australia **also has a **parliamentary system** of government, but it is a hybrid of the **British and American models.**
 
 
• The Australian Constitution was adopted in **1901 **and is based on the Westminster model of the British Parliament, but it also incorporates elements of **federalism and separation of powers.**

questions.question: Savitribai, together with her husband Jyotirao Phule, founded one of India's first girls' schools in Pune, at Bhide Wada in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1848.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Savitribai** and her husband **Jyotirao Phule** were **social reformers** who worked towards the **upliftment of women** and** lower-caste **communities in India.
 
• They founded one of India's first girls' schools in **Pune, Maharashtra, **which was established in **1848 at Bhide Wada**.
 
• The school aimed to provide **education to girls** who were otherwise denied access to learning opportunities due to** social and cultural **barriers.
 
• The school **faced opposition** from conservative elements in society, who believed that educating girls was against traditional values and norms.
 
• However, Savitribai and Jyotirao **persisted **in their efforts and continued to expand the school's reach.
 
• Over time, their work inspired the establishment of other **schools and educational institutions** for girls across India, and they are now widely recognized as pioneers of women's education in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Savitribai Phule was the **first female teacher in India** and played a significant role in promoting **women's education **in the country.
 
• She was also a** poet** and wrote several **poems on social issues** such as caste discrimination, women's rights, and education.
 
• Savitribai and Jyotirao Phule also established the **Satyashodhak Samaj,** a social reform organization that worked towards the emancipation of **lower-caste communities** in India.
 
• The couple faced **opposition and criticism **from conservative elements in society for their progressive views and actions, but they continued to work towards their goals with determination and courage.

questions.question: Except for the deep sea hydrothermal ecosystem, sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. What comes next in the energy food chain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **energy food chain **starts with the **sun**, which is the **primary source of energy** for all ecosystems on Earth.
 
• **Plants**, being the **primary producers,** are the next in the energy food chain.
 
• They use the sun's energy to produce food through** photosynthesis.**
 
• **Herbivores** come next in the chain, as they **consume plants **for their energy requirements.
 
• **Carnivores **come after herbivores, as they **consume other animals** for their energy requirements.
 
• Man is a** part** of the food chain, but not necessarily a next step.
 
• **Humans** can be herbivores or carnivores depending on their dietary habits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Herbivores** are animals that consume only plants as their **primary source of energy.**
 
• **Carnivores** are animals that consume other animals as their** primary source of energy.**
 
• **A food chain** is a straight line of living things that are eaten by other species to transfer **nutrients and energy.**
 
• Each organism in a food chain belongs to a distinct trophic level, which is determined by the number of energy transfers that separate it from the chain's fundamental input.

questions.question: In India, in the sphere of law making, a Bill does not become an Act unless it receives the assent of the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, a Bill passed by both the **Houses of Parliament **becomes an** Act** only after the **President **gives his **assent** to it.
 
• The Bill **does not** become law if the Governor or the President, as the case may be,** withholds** his assent.
 
• The President is the **head of the Indian state** and exercises his powers and functions through various **constitutional offices and authorities**, including the power to give assent to Bills passed by Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Attorney General** is the **chief legal advisor **to the government of India and provides legal advice to the government on various matters.
 
• The **Prime Minister **is the head of the government of India and exercises **executive powers.**
 
• The** Vice President **is the second-highest constitutional office in India and acts as the **ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha.**

questions.question: In _______, Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1526.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur **was a **Mongol prince** who founded the** Mughal Empire** in India in **1526** after **defeating Ibrahim Lodi**, the Sultan of Delhi, at the **battle of Panipat.**
 
• The battle of Panipat was a significant event in Indian history as it marked the **beginning of the Mughal Empire,** which lasted for more than 300 years and left a lasting impact on **Indian culture, art, and architecture.**
 
• Babur's victory at Panipat was mainly due to his **superior military tactics **and the** use of artillery**, which was a relatively new technology in India at that time.
 
• Babur's descendants, including **Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan**, continued to expand and consolidate the Mughal Empire, which reached its **zenith under Aurangzeb** in the late 17th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On **November 5, 1556**, the soldiers of **Samrat Hem Chandra Vikramaditya**, also known as Hemu, the Hindu king who ruled **North India** from Delhi, and the army of Akbar engaged in combat in the **Second Battle of Panipat. **
 
• For Akbar's generals, **Bairam Khan **and **Khan Zaman I**, it was an overwhelming triumph.
 
• Hemu was arrested, rendered nearly lifeless, and then **executed by Akbar, **who adopted the name Ghazi.

questions.question: The Food Corporation of India procures foodgrains from the farmers at the government announced __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**minimum support price.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Food Corporation of India **procures foodgrains from the **farmers** at the government announced **minimum support price.**
 
• The minimum support price is the price at which the government procures crops from the farmers to ensure that they get a** fair price** for their produce.
 
• The **Food Corporation of India** is the nodal agency.
 
• The minimum support price is announced by the government **every year before the sowing **season to ensure that farmers are incentivized to grow crops.
 
• The minimum support price is calculated based on factors such as the **cost of production, market price trends, **and other factors to ensure that farmers get a fair price for their produce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maximum Retail Price** is the **maximum price** at which a product can be **sold to the end consumer**.

 
 
• It is usually fixed by the manufacturer or the government to prevent retailers from **overcharging customers.**
 
 
 
• **Competitive Price** is the price at which a product is** sold in the market** based on the demand and supply dynamics.
 
 
• It is usually determined by the **market forces** and can fluctuate based on various factors such as **competition, seasonality, etc.**
 
 
 
• **Discounted Price** is the price at which a product is **sold at a lower price** than the market price.
 
 
• It is usually offered as a promotional offer or during a **sale to attract customers**.
 
• However, it is **no**t a sustainable pricing strategy in the long run.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of Propyne?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C₃H₄.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Propyne** is an **alkyne compound** that contains a** triple bond** between two carbon atoms.
 
• Its chemical formula is **C₃H₄**, which means it has **three carbon atoms **and **four hydrogen atoms.**
 
• Propyne is also known as **methylacetylene**, and it is used in the production of **synthetic rubber and plastics.**
 
• The correct chemical formula is important in understanding the **properties and behavior** of the compound in chemical reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **C₄H₅** is the chemical formula for **butyne.**

 
 
• It has **two** isomeric organic chemical components and **one triple bond.**
 
 
 
• **C₄H₄** is the chemical formula for **1,3-butadiene.**
 
 
• Though it can also be found in trace amounts in **fuel and polymers**, its primary application is in the manufacturing of **synthetic rubber.**
 
 
 
• **C₃H₅** is the chemical formula for **propene.**
 
 
• It is the second most basic hydrocarbon in the alkene class and possesses **one double bond. **

questions.question: An Act to protect children from offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography and provide for establishment of Special Courts, referred as _________ (POCSO).

options.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2013
Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
Protection of Child from Sexual Ordeal Act, 2012

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** POCSO Act** was enacted in** 2012** by the **Parliament of India **to protect children from **sexual offences **and provide a safe and secure environment for them.
 
• The act defines various sexual offences against children, such as **sexual assault, sexual harassment, and pornography,** and prescribes stringent punishments for the offenders.
 
• The act also provides for the establishment of **Special Courts** for the speedy trial of such offences and the appointment of **Special Public Prosecutors** to handle the cases.
 
• The act also has provisions for the protection of the** identity of the child victim**, the recording of the statement of the child in a** child-friendly manner, **and the provision of **medical and psychological support** to the child.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Parliament enacted the **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015,** despite strong opposition from the child rights community to several of its provisions.
 
• The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, which was in force before it was replaced, gave juvenile offenders in India who were between the ages of** 16 and 18** who had committed heinous offenses the opportunity to **face adult trials.**
 
• On** December 22, 2015**, the Rajya Sabha approved it. 
 
• The** Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Act, 2021,** which went into effect on **September 1, 2022**, further revised this act.

questions.question: Which of the following scientists is known as the father of the Green revolution in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M.S. Swaminathan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M.S. Swaminathan** is known as the **father of the Green Revolution** in India. 
 
• M.S. Swaminathan is an Indian** geneticist and agricultural scientist **who played a crucial role in the development of **high-yielding varieties of wheat, rice**, and other crops in India.
 
• He led the Indian team that successfully implemented the **Green Revolution in the 1960s,** which helped India achieve** self-sufficiency in food production** and averted a potential famine.
 
• Swaminathan's work on **plant genetics and breeding **helped to increase crop yields and improve the quality of crops, which in turn helped to alleviate **poverty, hunger, and malnutrition** in India and other developing countries.
 
• He has received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to agriculture, including the **World Food Prize, the Padma Shri, the Padma Bhushan, and the Padma Vibhushan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salim Ali** was an **Indian ornithologist** and **naturalist.**

 
 
• He is known as the **"Birdman of India" **for his contributions to the **study of birds **in India. 
 
 
 
• **Meghnad Saha **was an **Indian astrophysicist.**
 
 
• He is known for his work on the** thermal ionization of elements** and the **Saha equation. **
 
 
 
• **P.C. Mahalanobis **was an **Indian statistician** and **economist.**
 
 
• He is known for his work on the **Mahalanobis distance** and the development of the Indian Statistical Institute.

questions.question: Nearly ______ countries of the world are currently members of the WTO. (as on June 2014)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**160.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **160 countries** of the world are currently members of the WTO as of **June 2014.**
 
• The WTO (World Trade Organization) is an intergovernmental organization that regulates** international trade** between nations.
 
• It was established in **1995** and is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland.**
 
• The WTO provides a forum for member countries to negotiate and enforce **trade agreements, resolve disputes,** and** promote free trade.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to the **1994 Marrakesh Agreement**, the **World Trade Organization** (WTO) formally began operations on **January 1, 1995,** taking the place of the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade** (GATT), which had been founded in **1948. **
 
• The WTO is the** largest international economic organization** in the world, with **164 member states** that today account for more than** 98% of trade and GDP worldwide.**
 
• Members of the WTO contribute around** USD 220 million** annually toward the organization's budget, which is determined by their share of global commerce.

questions.question: Holi is the festival of colours, celebrated in the Hindu month of _______.

__

questions.question: Which place's distribution of pressure influences the weather conditions over India in winter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central and Western Asia.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Central and Western Asia** is known for the formation of a **high-pressure area** during **winters,** which causes **cold and dry winds** to blow towards India.
 
• These winds are known as the **northwestern winds** or the **'winter monsoon,'** and they bring in cold and dry air, resulting in a **decrease in temperature** over the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The high-pressure area over Central and Western Asia is caused due to the** cooling of the landmass **during winters.
 
• As the land cools down, the air above it also cools down and** becomes denser, **leading to the formation of **high pressure.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antarctica** is located at the **southernmost part of the Earth** and has little or **no influence **on the weather conditions over India in winter.
 
• Since they don't usually deliver significant weather,** winter monsoons** are less well-known.
 
 
• But they also blow a **lot of dry air** from the interior of a continent, which can cause **crop failure, drought, and water shortages. **
 
• The **northeast rains**, also known as the winter monsoon, are important in **Tamil Nadu, the Andhra Pradesh coast, Kerala**, the north of **Karnataka, and Lakshadweep.**

• The **2022 Paralympics winter games** were held in **Beijing, China.**

• **China** has hosted the **Paralympics summer games** twice before, in** 2008 and 1984,** but this was the first time they hosted the **Paralympics winter games.**

• However, they were **banned** from participating in the 2018 Winter Olympics due to a **doping scandal.**
